From a983aae397767e9da931128ff2b5bf9066513ce3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Pavel Begunkov <asml.silence@gmail.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 22:19:32 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] io_uring/zcrx: fix sgtable leak on mapping failures

In an unlikely case when io_populate_area_dma() fails, which could only
happen on a PAGE_POOL_32BIT_ARCH_WITH_64BIT_DMA machine,
io_zcrx_map_area() will have an initialised and not freed table. It was
supposed to be cleaned up in the error path, but !is_mapped prevents
that.

Fixes: 439a98b972fbb ("io_uring/zcrx: deduplicate area mapping")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Signed-off-by: Pavel Begunkov <asml.silence@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

diff --git a/io_uring/zcrx.c b/io_uring/zcrx.c
index 69567e19b4ca..006e1bfefa5f 100644
--- a/io_uring/zcrx.c
+++ b/io_uring/zcrx.c
@@ -288,6 +288,9 @@ static int io_zcrx_map_area(struct io_zcrx_ifq *ifq, struct io_zcrx_area *area)
 	}
 
 	ret = io_populate_area_dma(ifq, area);
+	if (ret && !area->mem.is_dmabuf)
+		dma_unmap_sgtable(ifq->dev, &area->mem.page_sg_table,
+				  DMA_FROM_DEVICE, IO_DMA_ATTR);
 	if (ret == 0)
 		area->is_mapped = true;
 	return ret;
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a memory leak in `io_uring/zcrx` where a scatter-gather table (sgtable) was not properly cleaned up when a DMA mapping failed.

## Modifications in `io_uring/zcrx.c`

- **Added a `dma_unmap_sgtable()` call** in `io_zcrx_map_area()` that executes when `io_populate_area_dma()` fails **and** the area is **not** a dmabuf (`!area->mem.is_dmabuf`). This unmaps the sgtable that was previously initialized during the mapping attempt.

- This new cleanup code is placed **before** the success/return check, ensuring it runs even on failure.

## Relationship

The bug occurred because the original code only set `area->is_mapped = true` on success. On failure, `is_mapped` remained `false`, which prevented any later cleanup logic (that checked `is_mapped`) from freeing the sgtable. The fix directly performs the necessary `dma_unmap_sgtable()` on the error path (excluding dmabufs, which use a different mapping mechanism) to avoid leaking the sgtable memory and DMA resources. This ensures that the sgtable is always freed when `io_populate_area_dma()` fails, preventing a resource leak on architectures with `PAGE_POOL_32BIT_ARCH_WITH_64BIT_DMA`.

Here is the commit message:
io_uring/zcrx: fix sgtable leak on mapping failures

In an unlikely case when io_populate_area_dma() fails, which could only
happen on a PAGE_POOL_32BIT_ARCH_WITH_64BIT_DMA machine,
io_zcrx_map_area() will have an initialised and not freed table. It was
supposed to be cleaned up in the error path, but !is_mapped prevents
that.

Fixes: 439a98b972fbb ("io_uring/zcrx: deduplicate area mapping")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>
Signed-off-by: Pavel Begunkov <asml.silence@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

Here is the root cause:
The sgtable is initialized before calling io_populate_area_dma(), but the cleanup on failure depends on the `is_mapped` flag, which is set only after success. On failure, `is_mapped` remains false, so the cleanup code that checks this flag does not execute, causing the sgtable to leak.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int io_zcrx_map_area(struct io_zcrx_ifq *ifq, struct io_zcrx_area *area)
 {
 	int ret;
 
 	guard(mutex)(&ifq->pp_lock);
 	if (area->is_mapped)
 		return 0;
 
 	if (!area->mem.is_dmabuf) {
 		ret = dma_map_sgtable(ifq->dev, &area->mem.page_sg_table,
 				      DMA_FROM_DEVICE, IO_DMA_ATTR);
 		if (ret < 0)
 			return ret;
 	}
 
 	ret = io_populate_area_dma(ifq, area);
+	if (ret && !area->mem.is_dmabuf)
+		dma_unmap_sgtable(ifq->dev, &area->mem.page_sg_table,
+				  DMA_FROM_DEVICE, IO_DMA_ATTR);
 	if (ret == 0)
 		area->is_mapped = true;
 	return ret;
 }
